chunks: Ibn Mahbub, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام: concerning

Four men testified against a muhsan man for zina, then one of them retracted after the man had been killed. He said: “If the one who retracts says, ‘I was mistaken,’ he is given the hadd punishment and made liable for the blood-money; but if he says, ‘I did it deliberately,’ he is killed.”

key_terms.أَوْهَمْتُ: I was mistaken or under an error
key_terms.الدِّيَةَ: the blood-money owed for wrongful killing
key_terms.الرَّاجِعُ: the witness who retracts his testimony
key_terms.بِالزِّنَى: for zina, meaning unlawful sexual intercourse
key_terms.مُحْصَنٍ: a legally protected married person subject to the ruling discussed here

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a witness retracts testimony after a person was executed for zina?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning false testimony in a capital case of zina against a muhsan person. It distinguishes between mistaken testimony and deliberate false testimony, assigning hadd and financial liability in the first case, and execution in the second due to intentional causation of wrongful killing.
